title: What Fusion Micro-Reactors Is
definition: Fusion Micro-Reactors: neighborhood-scale fusion power plants.
description:
Fusion Micro-Reactors is neighborhood-scale fusion power plants. It sits squarely in Future Energy Systems, the frontier where compact magnets science becomes reactor logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are safety cases-scale. Societies that master reactor hulls early will shape mass manufacturing practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why compact magnets programs worldwide now treat Fusion Micro-Reactors as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Fusion Micro-Reactors needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

title: Real Research Today: Fusion Micro-Reactors
definition: Today's documented research behind Fusion Micro-Reactors.
description:
The road to Fusion Micro-Reactors is already being paved. Space-based solar power studies (Caltech SSPP, ESA SOLARIS) test beaming power from orbit. Commonwealth Fusion Systems is building SPARC, a compact high-field tokamak aiming for net energy.

Green hydrogen electrolyzer capacity is scaling under EU and US clean-hydrogen programs. Together these programs form the compact magnets foundation that Fusion Micro-Reactors will build on — the reactor logistics results, the mass manufacturing methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as reactor logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Fusion Micro-Reactors
definition: Estimates Fusion Micro-Reactors readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Fusion Micro-Reactors components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a reactor hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Fusion Micro-Reactors Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Fusion Micro-Reactors operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Fusion Micro-Reactors installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 1608 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where compact magnets monitoring, reactor logistics redundancy, or mass manufacturing maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Fusion Micro-Reactors Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Fusion Micro-Reactors: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Fusion Micro-Reactors — neighborhood-scale fusion power plants.

Phase 1 — Prove (compact magnets): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (reactor logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (mass manufacturing): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (safety cases): reactor hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and neighborhoods-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
